text:
Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández comments on voter rights and constituent services in latest tweets
Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, who represents New Mexico’s 3rd district in the U.S. Congress, recently posted a series of updates on her official Twitter account, addressing constituent services and commenting on recent political developments.
On September 14, 2026, Rep. Leger Fernández informed constituents about available assistance with federal agencies: "Do you need help with a federal agency? My office can help with Social Security benefits, veteran benefits, tax returns, and more! Stop by our walk-in hours tomorrow in Jemez Springs."
Later that evening, she reacted to a Supreme Court decision regarding mail-in voting: "A win for voters and for democracy. The Supreme Court just blocked the Trump administration from illegally restricting mail-in voting using the Postal Service. President Trump can’t make it harder for you to vote just because he’s scared of how you’ll vote." This post came amid ongoing national debates over election laws and access.
On September 15, Rep. Leger Fernández addressed recent rhetoric from former President Donald Trump: "Trump is using “New America” as a distraction from his corruption, rising prices and growing unpopularity. New Mexico existed long before Trump and will continue long after him."
Leger Fernández has served in Congress since 2021 after succeeding Ben Ray Luján. She was born in Las Vegas, New Mexico, in 1959 and resides in Santa Fe. In past elections, she defeated Sharon Clahchischilliage in 2024 as well as Alexis Martinez Johnson in both the 2020 and 2022 general elections.
